title: Company-wide Policies & Processes (Access, Change, Data, Procurement, Vendor Management, Travel, Templates)
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview

This document is the canonical reference for company-wide policies and operational processes that apply to Redwood Inference employees and contractors. It covers: access and permissions, change management, data management, procurement and expenses, vendor management, travel policies, and common internal templates. The goal is to centralize expectations, approval flows, and standard forms so teams have a consistent, auditable workplace process.

Scope

- Applies to all full-time employees, contractors, and vendors with access to company systems or assets.
- Operational exceptions must be documented and approved by the owning team and People Ops or Finance-Legal as appropriate.

Summary of Key Principles

1) Least privilege: Grant the minimum access required for a role or task.
2) Separation of duties: Approvals (requestor, manager, approver) must be distinct where risk is elevated.
3) Auditability: All access and procurement actions must have a traceable ticket or PO number.
4) Risk-based controls: Higher risk/data requires stricter controls (2FA, restricted networks, additional approvals).

1) Access & Permissions

Purpose: Standardize how identities are provisioned and governed.

Ownership and tools:
- Identity provider: Okta (SSO + SCIM for provisioning).
- Directory group management: GitHub org teams, GCP IAM groups, AWS IAM roles where applicable.
- Audit logs stored in Splunk/Datadog for 365 days (see Security and Compliance policy).

Access types and examples:
- Short-term access (SSH bastion, admin console): request via access-request template and set expiry (max 7 days unless approved).
- Role-based access: request via Okta group assignment; manager approval required.
- Production emergency access: Jira incident + post-hoc approval within 24 hours.

Request process (standard)
1. Create an "Access Request" in Jira (project: ACCESS). Include: user email, role, resources, justification, expiration date.
2. Manager approves in Jira; automated Okta workflow assigns group.
3. Owner team verifies access within 48 hours.
4. Access is auto-revoked on expiry; People Ops runs quarterly access recertification.

Access review cadence:
- Quarterly role recertification (People Ops and team owners).
- Monthly automated orphan account cleanup (accounts with no activity for 90+ days flagged).

Least-privilege examples and guardrails:
- No service account should be used for interactive login.
- Admin privileges require 2FA and MFA enforcement.
- GCP project-level editors are restricted to infra-oncall and infra-admin groups.

2) Change Management

Purpose: Ensure safe, auditable changes to production and shared infrastructure.

Change categories:
- Standard (low risk) - pre-approved routine ops (config updates, patching with automated pipeline).
- Normal (medium risk) - scheduled changes that require documented plan and peer review.
- Emergency (high risk) - immediate fixes for outages; requires post-change review.

Change window and SLAs:
- Normal changes scheduled during the standard change window: Mon-Fri 02:00-04:00 PT for infra-facing actions.
- Emergency changes: must be communicated on #oncall and in the incident channel.

Change request template (YAML example):

---
title: "Change: <short description>"
owner: "<owner-name>"
risk: "low|medium|high"
start_window: "YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM PT"
rollback_plan: "<steps to rollback>"
validation_steps:
  - "<step 1>"
  - "<step 2>"
---

Approval flow:
1. Create change request in Jira (project: CHANGE). Attach rollout plan and impact analysis.
2. Peer review by at least one engineer not on the change team.
3. Approver (team lead or designated approver for service) signs off.
4. Schedule and execute. Post-change validation performed and documented.

Emergency process:
1. Execute emergency change and update the ticket.
2. Notify SRE and People Ops immediately.
3. Conduct a post-incident review within 5 business days; document lessons and action items.

Rollback/Canary policy:
- Use canary rollouts for model deployments and configuration changes.
- Automatic rollback if error rate > 2% or latency > 2x baseline during a 10-minute window.

3) Data Management

Data classification levels:
- PUBLIC: data safe for public distribution.
- INTERNAL: default for internal docs and telemetry.
- CONFIDENTIAL: customer PII, contracts, internal legal or financials.
- RESTRICTED: regulated data (PHI, financial account numbers) - requires additional controls.

Handling rules:
- Encryption: All CONFIDENTIAL and RESTRICTED data must be encrypted at rest (KMS) and in transit (TLS 1.2+).
- Storage: Use approved storage buckets with access limited by IAM. No local storage of restricted data on developer laptops.
- Copying and sharing: Avoid exporting data to third-party SaaS without vendor assessment.

Retention and deletion:
- Default telemetry retention: 90 days.
- Backups: encrypted backups retained per service SLA (minimum 30 days; critical DBs 90 days).
- Data deletion requests: follow the Data Deletion Runbook (linked in related_pages).

Auditing and monitoring:
- Data access audits run weekly and anomalous access alerts routed to the security team.
- Egress monitoring for large downloads (>1GB) triggers investigation.

4) Procurement & Expenses

Purpose: Standardize purchasing, vendor contracts, and employee reimbursable expenses.

Purchasing channels and thresholds:
| Amount (USD) | Approval required | Purchase method | Owner |
|-------------:|------------------|----------------|-------|
| < 1,000 | Manager | Expense report / P-card | Employee Manager |
| 1,000 - 10,000 | Manager + Finance | Purchase Order via Coupa | Finance Ops |
| > 10,000 | Director + Finance Legal | Contract + PO | Finance Lead |

Vendor onboarding checklist (summary):
1. Confirm business need and budget.
2. Security questionnaire (must pass or have remediations).
3. Finance creates PO and issues payment terms.
4. Legal signs contract.
5. Add vendor to vendor inventory and assign owner.

Expense reimbursement:
- Submit expenses via Ramp with receipts attached within 30 days.
- Per-diem: see Travel section. Cards are reconciled weekly by Finance.

Procurement lifecycle steps (numbered):
1. Requestor opens a procurement request (Coupa).
2. Budget owner approves.
3. Security/legal review if the vendor handles sensitive data.
4. Finance issues PO and completes onboarding.

5) Vendor Management

Risk assessment: All vendors classified as Low/Medium/High risk. High risk vendors (store/process CONFIDENTIAL or RESTRICTED data) must provide SOC2 Type II report or equivalent and pass a security questionnaire.

Vendor review cadence:
- High risk: annual review.
- Medium risk: biennial review.
- Low risk: review on contract renewal.

Offboarding a vendor:
1. Revoke access (Okta groups, API keys, cloud roles).
2. Ensure data transfer or secure deletion per contract.
3. Close PO and archive contract.

6) Travel Policy (summary)

Booking and approval:
- All travel must be pre-approved via the Travel Request template and get manager sign-off for trips > $1,000.
- Use company travel portal (Concur) or approved travel agents for corporate bookings.

Expenses and per-diem:
- Meals: up to $75/day in NA markets (higher local allowances for high-cost cities).
- Lodging: book standard business rate unless pre-approved.
- International travel: employees must register travel in the travel portal for safety notifications.

Safety and insurance:
- Company covers standard business travel insurance; People Ops should be notified of high-risk travel.

7) Internal Templates & Where to Find Them

The following templates are maintained in the Templates space (linked in related_pages):
- Access Request (Jira template)
- Change Request (YAML/Jira template)
- Vendor Onboarding Checklist (spreadsheet)
- Procurement Request (Coupa form)
- Travel Request and Expense Template (Concur / Ramp)
- Post-Change Validation Checklist (Markdown)

Quick examples (Access Request summary):
- Fields: user_email, requested_groups, justification, expiration_date, manager_approval.
- Auto-workflow: When manager_approval = true, Okta SCIM adds to the requested group.

Common Procedures (step-by-step)

A) Requesting access (standard)
1. Open ACCESS Jira ticket with required fields.
2. Manager approves.
3. System provisions via Okta within 4 hours.
4. Owner verifies access and tags ticket for audit.

B) Performing a normal change
1. Create CHANGE ticket and attach rollout and rollback plan.
2. Peer review and approver sign-off.
3. Schedule in change window and execute runbook.
4. Validate and close ticket.

C) Procuring a new vendor (summary)
1. Submit Coupa procurement request with justification and budget code.
2. Security questionnaire if data handling is involved.
3. Legal reviews and signs the contract.
4. Finance issues PO and marks vendor active.

Escalation & Exceptions

- For cross-team disputes (access, budget, or legal) escalate to the function owner and People Ops.
- Emergency exceptions to any policy must be documented in Jira and retro-reviewed within 5 business days.

Ownership & Contacts

- People Ops: policy ownership, access recertification, travel approvals. (people-ops@redwood.ai)
- Finance: purchasing, card management, PO issuance. (finance@redwood.ai)
- Security: data classification, vendor risk, audits. (security@redwood.ai)
- Eng-infra / SRE: change windows, runbooks, production access. (oncall@redwood.ai)

Appendices

A. Useful links:
- Change request template: /confluence/eng-platform/change-request-template
- Access request template: /confluence/policies-and-process/access-request-template
- Vendor security questionnaire: /confluence/security-and-compliance/vendor-security-questionnaire

B. Example rollback command (illustrative)
- To rollback a Kubernetes deployment to revision N:
  kubectl rollout undo deployment/<service-name> --to-revision=N -n <namespace>

C. Audit & retention notes:
- Procurement records retained for 7 years for accounting and audit.
- Access and authentication logs retained for 365 days unless otherwise required.
